# Watch-Loop Requirements Quality Checklist: fcon watch mode

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of the watch-loop domain — rebuild pipeline, live viewer refresh, failure/recovery semantics — as specified in spec.md and designed in plan.md
**Created**: 2026-08-26
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) | [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness — Rebuild Pipeline

- [ ] CHK001 - Is the exact set of watched inputs (file extensions, directories, exclusions) specified in requirements, or delegated with a binding reference to the plan? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, Plan §R-003]
- [ ] CHK002 - Are requirements defined for the initial-build failure case — watcher and viewer still start, or session aborts with which exit code? [Gap, Spec §FR-001 vs contracts/cli-watch.md exit 130]
- [ ] CHK003 - Is the required behavior when no `build.command` is configured specified (error text, exit code, hint) for `fcon watch` specifically? [Completeness, Gap]
- [ ] CHK004 - Are requirements specified for a build that succeeds but produces empty output (distinct from build exit != 0)? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK005 - Is the maximum snapshot age / staleness bound during a long-running failed-build period specified or explicitly unconstrained? [Gap, Non-Functional]

## Requirement Completeness — Viewer Refresh

- [ ] CHK006 - Is the refresh mechanism requirement (FR-004) written mechanism-neutrally so polling vs push remains a plan decision, and does the plan's polling choice stay within the stated NFR-001 budget? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004/NFR-001, Plan §R-002]
- [ ] CHK007 - Are requirements defined for viewer behavior while the SPA tab is backgrounded (browser timer throttling) relative to the 2 s propagation target? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §NFR-001]
- [ ] CHK008 - Are requirements defined for multiple browser tabs viewing the same watch session — all tabs update, or last-tab-wins? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is the error-indication placement and persistence in the viewer specified (banner vs overlay, dismissible vs auto-clear on recovery)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK010 - Is "debounced" quantified (window value or plan reference) so FR-002 can be objectively verified? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §FR-002/NFR-001]
- [ ] CHK011 - Is "exactly one follow-up build" (FR-003) unambiguous about whether further edits during the follow-up re-queue? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003/EDGE-002]
- [ ] CHK012 - Is "visible error indication" (FR-006) specified measurably enough to pass/reject AC-004 without taste judgment? [Measurability, Spec §FR-006/AC-004]
- [ ] CHK013 - Is the Ctrl+C exit code requirement (FR-008, exit 0) reconciled with the CLI's existing second-signal hard-exit-130 convention? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, contracts/cli-watch.md]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK014 - Do exit-code requirements across FR-001/FR-006/FR-008 and contracts/cli-watch.md form a single non-overlapping table (session-termination codes vs build-failure non-exit)? [Consistency]
- [ ] CHK015 - Is COMP-001 ("validate --watch unchanged") consistent with any shared refactoring of WatchRunner into WatchSession — preserved behavior stated as a requirement, not just an assumption? [Consistency, Gap, Spec §COMP-001, Plan §R-005]
- [ ] CHK016 - Is the viewer-degradation requirement (plain `fcon view` sessions have no `/api/status`) specified as a requirement, or only in the plan/contract? [Gap, Spec §COMP-001 vs contracts/cli-watch.md]

## Scenario Coverage — Exception & Recovery

- [ ] CHK017 - Are recovery requirements defined for each failure mode: build failure (ERR-001), invalid snapshot (ERR-002), input deleted/renamed (ERR-003) — including who detects recovery and how the viewer learns of it? [Coverage, Spec §ERR-001..003]
- [ ] CHK018 - Are requirements defined for watch-input reappearance after deletion (ERR-003 "if the platform permits") — is the fallback (instruct restart) acceptable per the spec's own measurability bar? [Ambiguity, Spec §ERR-003]
- [ ] CHK019 - Are second-watch-session-on-same-directory requirements specified beyond "must fail with a clear message" — exit code, port conflict vs lock semantics? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK020 - Are requirements defined for `bin/`/`obj/` build outputs triggering rebuild loops (self-triggering feedback), given the build writes inside the watched tree? [Gap, Edge Case, Plan §R-003]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK021 - Are the NFR-001 latency budget components (debounce value, build time unbounded, propagation < 2 s) each individually testable, and is the unbounded build time explicitly accepted? [Measurability, Spec §NFR-001]
- [ ] CHK022 - Are resource-bound requirements specified for a long session (watcher handle leaks, child-process accumulation on cancelled builds)? [Gap, Non-Functional, Spec §FR-008/NFR-002]
- [ ] CHK023 - Is the loopback-only security requirement (FR-007) testable as written (which interfaces, what counts as unreachable)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-007/AC-007]

## Constitution and Traceability

- [ ] CHK024 - Current source and nearest instructions were inspected; stale sources are resolved explicitly
- [ ] CHK025 - Repository ownership, licensing, security, and compatibility boundaries are testable
- [ ] CHK026 - Requirements and acceptance criteria have stable identifiers with no material clarification markers
- [ ] CHK027 - Each requirement/risk traces to tasks and planned verification evidence (tasks.md pending — verify after `/speckit-tasks`)
- [ ] CHK028 - Local focused/full commands, prerequisites, failures, and exclusions are explicit
- [ ] CHK029 - Independent review and named human gate ownership are defined
